name: Minnesota
agency: Minnesota Department of Public Safety, Driver and Vehicle Services (DVS)
permitAge: 15 (instruction permit; minors must have started classroom driver education and need a parent signature)

teen.supervisedHours: 50 hours including 15 at night, or 40 hours including 15 at night if a parent completes the supplemental parent class (DPS log form; Minn. Stat. 171.055)
teen.holdPermit: 6 months immediately before applying, with no moving, crash-related or alcohol/drug convictions (Minn. Stat. 171.055)
teen.nightLimit: Provisional license, first 6 months: no driving midnight to 5 a.m. unless with a licensed driver 25 or older, or driving between home and work (AAA Minneapolis)
teen.passengerLimit: First 6 months: at most one passenger under 20 who is not immediate family; months 7 to 12: at most three; ends after 12 months (dmvroads, secondary)
teen.phone: Instruction permit and provisional license holders under 18: no cell phone use while moving, hand-held or hands-free (Minn. Stat. 171.05, 171.055). All drivers: hands-free law since Aug. 1, 2019 (voice or one-touch only).

notes: Permit supervisor for a driver under 18: licensed driver 21 or older in the front passenger seat (Hennepin County).

Knowledge test passing score 80 percent (Minn. R. 7410.4760). Third-party sites say 40 questions (32 correct); not confirmed by DVS, so left null. DVS gives knowledge tests in Spanish (Sahan Journal reports 113,587 Spanish tests Oct 2023 - Sep 2024).

Ted Foss Move Over law (Minn. Stat. 169.18): move one full lane away from stopped emergency, maintenance, construction or tow vehicles with flashing lights; since 2023 also stalled vehicles with hazards on.
School bus (Minn. Stat. 169.444): stop at least 20 feet away; oncoming traffic need not stop only on separated roadways (physical barrier, raised or depressed median); snowbanks do not count.
Speed (Minn. Stat. 169.14, 2007 text): 30 mph urban district, 70 mph on interstates outside urbanized areas over 50,000, 65 mph inside them.
Headlights required whenever it is raining, snowing, sleeting or hailing (Minn. Stat. 169.48; DPS blog).
No-fault insurance: liability 30/60/10, PIP $40,000, UM/UIM 25/50 (secondary sources).
